hubs.name: hub_business_entity
hubs.description: Company-wide party register (customers, vendors, employees, stores, persons). Persons share the same business entity number, so person data attaches here as satellites rather than a separate hub. Email addresses and credentials are keyed by the same number and are declared as feeds so their satellites bind to their own source.

hubs.name: hub_address
hubs.description: Postal address recorded once and shareable by many parties.

hubs.name: hub_address_type
hubs.description: Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping).

hubs.name: hub_contact_type
hubs.description: Reference list of contact roles.

hubs.name: hub_phone_number_type
hubs.description: Reference list of phone number types (home, work, mobile).

hubs.name: hub_country_region
hubs.description: Countries and regions identified by ISO code.

hubs.name: hub_state_province
hubs.description: States and provinces identified by their own number.

hubs.name: hub_department
hubs.description: Register of departments, the organisational units in which people work. Keyed on the stable DepartmentID because department names can change.

hubs.name: hub_shift
hubs.description: Register of eight-hour working shifts. Keyed on the stable ShiftID because shift names and definitions can be adjusted.

hubs.name: hub_job_candidate

links.name: link_business_entity_address
links.description: Which addresses a party uses and in what capacity; party+address+type is unique.

links.name: link_business_entity_contact
links.description: Organisation (business entity) to the person acting as its contact, in a contact role; organisation+person+role is unique.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_details
satellites.description: Business entity register last-changed timestamp; rowguid excluded as technical replication metadata.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_name
satellites.description: Person type and name details with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Ordinary name/contact PII; carries the Person ModifiedDate once.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_marketing_consent
satellites.description: Email promotion consent level, historised for audit.
satellites.split_rationale: Consent is a distinct classification with its own audit need and rate of change.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_sensitive
satellites.description: Sensitive XML additional contact info and demographics, access-restricted.
satellites.split_rationale: Sensitive data classification restricted separately from name reporting.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_credential
satellites.description: Existence and last-change of a sign-in credential only; hash and salt are excluded.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source; credential values excluded from the warehouse.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email
satellites.description: All email addresses of a person, numbered within the person, historised.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source at finer grain, several concurrent rows per person.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone_number_type_phones
satellites.description: Telephone numbers of a person per phone type, historised.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of party-address relationships.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_contact_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of contact relationships.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street, city and postal details, historised.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of the address.
satellites.split_rationale: Distinct data type (spatial) and sensitive classification.

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type name.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type name.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State/province code, no-genuine-code flag and name.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory
satellites.description: Sales territory assignment of the state/province, historised; territory descriptions come from the sales area.
satellites.split_rationale: Territory assignment changes at a different rate and needs separate history tracking.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_details
satellites.description: Non-sensitive employee details: job title, hire date, salaried/hourly flag, active status and network login. Changes are kept so values that the source overwrites still have a history.
satellites.split_rationale: General employment attributes that change slowly and are not restricted; holds the single ModifiedDate audit column for Employee.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_sensitive
satellites.description: Personal and sensitive employee attributes, with access limited to authorised HR users.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by data classification (PII) so that access can be restricted.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave
satellites.description: Point-in-time readings of vacation and sick-leave balances. Keeping each change shows how balances move over time.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by rate of change: balances change much more often than other employee attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and level in the organisational hierarchy. History is captured as changes occur.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position is its own concern and changes on a different schedule from other attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_pay_history
satellites.description: Pay rate history. RateChangeDate (the effective date) separates the concurrent records.
satellites.split_rationale: Comes from a separate source table at a finer grain (one row per rate change). EmployeePayHistory is now declared as a feed of hub_business_entity.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of each department/shift assignment. An assignment with no end date is the current one.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_audit
satellites.description: When each assignment record was last updated, used to judge how current it is.
satellites.split_rationale: The audit timestamp is kept apart from the effectivity dates.

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department name, group membership and last-change date. History is kept for as-was reporting.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift name and start/end times. History is kept because definitions can be adjusted.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_resume
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé, stored as a structured document. It is non-employee personal data, subject to its own retention rules.

evidence: Product.ProductNumber is 'Unique product identification number'. No existing hub models products; the hubs cover business entity, address, contact/phone/address types, country, state, department, shift and job candidate.
Product.ProductID is the primary key of Product. No existing hub has a product business key. It is referenced as a foreign key by many new tables but not by the existing vault.
Product.Name is a descriptive attribute of the new Product entity, not an identifier. No existing hub or satellite carries product names. Same-named columns on other tables are not evidence.
ProductCategory.Name is 'Category description', an attribute of the new ProductCategory entity. Nothing in the vault models categories.
ProductCategory.ProductCategoryID is its own primary key. No existing hub has this key.
ProductSubcategory.Name is 'Subcategory description', an attribute of the new subcategory entity. No existing construct models it.
ProductSubcategory.ProductSubcategoryID is its own primary key. No existing hub has this key.
ProductModel.Name is 'Product model description', an attribute of the new ProductModel entity. No existing construct models it.
ProductModel.ProductModelID is its own primary key. No existing hub has this key.
Culture.CultureID (nchar(6)) is a primary key. The vault has no culture or language hub. hub_country_region is keyed by CountryRegionCode, and no cross-reference ties the two.
Culture.Name is 'Culture description', an attribute of the new Culture entity. It is not an identifier of any existing hub.
UnitMeasure.UnitMeasureCode (nchar(3)) is a primary key. No existing hub models units of measure.
UnitMeasure.Name is 'Unit of measure description', an attribute of the new entity. Nothing existing matches it.
ProductDescription.ProductDescriptionID is its own primary key. No existing hub models product descriptions.
ProductPhoto.ProductPhotoID is its own primary key. No existing photo or image hub.
Illustration.IllustrationID is its own primary key. It holds manufacturing diagrams, and nothing existing models them.

Document.DocumentNode (hierarchyid) is the primary key of Document. No existing hub models documents. Document.Owner points to Employee.BusinessEntityID, which only gives a link to hub_business_entity, not an identity.
Document.rowguid is a ROWGUIDCOL for FileStream, an alternate unique identifier of the new Document entity. No existing hub uses a GUID key.
Document.FileName is a descriptive attribute of the new Document entity, not a key of any existing hub.
Location.Name is 'Location description' for a manufacturing location, an attribute of the new Location entity. It is not hub_address, which is keyed by AddressID and models postal addresses.

Location.LocationID (smallint) is the key of a manufacturing/inventory location, with CostRate and Availability in hours. hub_address is keyed by AddressID and no cross-reference connects them. The shared word 'location' alone is not evidence.
ScrapReason.Name is 'Failure description', an attribute of the new ScrapReason entity. Nothing existing matches it.
ScrapReason.ScrapReasonID is its own primary key. No existing hub models scrap reasons.
WorkOrder.WorkOrderID is the work order key. No existing hub models manufacturing work orders.

The composite key WorkOrderID + ProductID + OperationSequence identifies an operation step on a work order. Nothing in the vault has this grain. It will probably become a link or a hub depending on modelling.

TransactionHistory.TransactionID is the primary key of product inventory transactions. The vault has no transaction construct. TransactionHistoryArchive has the same shape but is a separate table, not an existing vault construct.
ProductReview.ProductReviewID is its own primary key. ReviewerName and EmailAddress are free text, with no business-entity key linking them to the existing hub_business_entity.
The composite key of product, location, shelf and bin is the grain of stock held. No existing construct has this key.
The key is built from two Product.ProductID foreign keys (assembly and component) plus StartDate. Nothing existing models product structure.

requirements.text: The business must be able to identify every product uniquely and unambiguously.
Each product carries a product number that is unique and serves as the natural business key used to refer to a product in day-to-day work.
Every product must carry a product name.
The product name is descriptive, is not guaranteed to be unique, and must not be relied on to identify a product.
The business must know, for every product, whether it is manufactured in-house or purchased from outside.
Whether a product is manufactured in-house or purchased determines whether it has a manufacturing route, a bill of materials and work orders, or whether it arrives via purchasing.
The business must know whether a product is a salable item or not.
Reporting on the product portfolio must be able to separate salable finished goods from internal-only items such as components and sub-assemblies.
The business must track product colour where it applies, since not all products have a colour.
The business must track product size as a short code or value, together with the unit of measure in which the size is expressed.
requirements.obj: product size and size unit of measure

requirements.text: Product size and its unit of measure must always be read together.
The business must track product weight and, separately, the unit of measure in which the weight is expressed.
requirements.obj: product weight and weight unit of measure

requirements.text: A product weight figure is meaningless without its unit and must always be read together with it.
The business must know how many days are required to manufacture a product, to support lead-time planning and promise dates.
Products are grouped into a product line, and the lines recognised are Road, Mountain, Touring and Standard.
Reporting on the product range, on sales performance and on manufacturing load must be possible by product line.
requirements.obj: range, sales performance and manufacturing load by product line

requirements.text: Products carry a class of High, Medium or Low.
The business meaning of product class is not stated in the source system and its definition must be confirmed with the product management team before it is used as an analytical dimension.
Products carry a style of Womens, Mens or Universal.
Product style is a merchandising attribute and must be available for analysis of the range.
The business must record the standard cost of a product, which is the cost figure used for costing and margin purposes.
The business must record the list price of a product, which is the price at which it is offered for sale.
The business must be able to compare list price against standard cost to understand the margin position of each product.
The business must record the safety stock level for each product, being the minimum inventory quantity intended to be held.
The business must record the reorder point for each product, being the inventory level at which a purchase order or a work order is triggered.

The business must be able to compare actual inventory on hand against the safety stock level and the reorder point, to identify products at risk of stock-out and products where a replenishment action is overdue.
requirements.obj: inventory on hand against safety stock level and reorder point

requirements.text: The business must know the date from which a product became available for sale.
The business must know the date from which a product ceased to be available for sale, where that has happened; a current product has no such date.
The business must know the date on which a product was discontinued, where applicable.
Discontinuation and the end of sale availability are recorded separately and must be treated as two distinct business events, with the difference in meaning to be confirmed by product management.
The business must be able to report on the active product range as at any point in time using the sell start and sell end dates, for example which products were sellable in March of last year.
requirements.obj: active product range as at a point in time

requirements.text: Products are organised into a two-level classification consisting of product categories, which are subdivided into product subcategories.
A product category must be identifiable by its name (its description); categories are the top level of the merchandising hierarchy, such as bikes, components, clothing and accessories.
A product subcategory must be identifiable by its name.
A product subcategory belongs to exactly one product category.
A product belongs to at most one subcategory.
Not every product is placed in a subcategory, since components and internal items may sit outside the merchandising hierarchy.
Reporting must handle unclassified products gracefully rather than dropping them.
The business must be able to roll up any product-level measure, such as inventory, cost, price, transaction volume and scrap, to subcategory and then to category level.
requirements.obj: product-level measures to subcategory and category

requirements.text: The business must be able to identify a product model by its name.
Several individual products, such as different sizes and colours of the same bicycle, can share one product model.
A product belongs to at most one product model.
Not every product has a product model.
The business must be able to group and report products by product model, as this is the level at which design, catalogue content and manufacturing instructions are held.
Detailed catalogue information is held at product model level in a structured document format, and the business needs this content available for catalogue and web publication.
Manufacturing instructions are held at product model level in a structured document format, and manufacturing and quality teams need access to the instructions that apply to a given model.
The level of detail that can be extracted from the structured manufacturing instruction documents needs to be scoped separately with the manufacturing engineering team.
The business maintains a library of product descriptions, which are free-text marketing descriptions held independently of any one product.
The business maintains a list of cultures (language and locale designations), each identified by a short culture code and carrying a descriptive name.
A product model is associated with a product description in a specific culture, so that the same model can have different descriptions for different markets.
The business must be able to report which product models have catalogue descriptions in which cultures.
The business must be able to identify product models that are missing a description in a culture the business sells into, as a content-completeness check for marketing.
requirements.obj: product models missing a description in a culture

requirements.text: The combination of product model, product description and culture is the meaningful business fact, since a description is only useful when it is known which model it describes and in which language.
The business maintains a library of product photographs.
Each photograph exists in a small (thumbnail) version and a large version, and each version has its own image file and file name.
A product may have several photographs, and a photograph may be used for more than one product.
For each product, one photograph is designated the principal image.
The business must be able to identify the principal image for a product, as it is used as the lead image in the catalogue and on the web.
The business must be able to identify products that have no photograph at all.
The business must be able to identify products that have photographs but no designated principal image.
The business maintains a set of illustrations used in manufacturing instructions, which are technical diagrams held in a structured format.
An illustration is associated with one or more product models, and a product model may have several illustrations.
The business must be able to determine which illustrations support which product models, so that manufacturing documentation can be assembled and kept complete.
The business holds a controlled document library that is organised hierarchically, with documents inside folders, and that carries approval and revision control.
The business must be able to identify each document in the library and know its title.
The business must know whether an entry in the library is a folder or an actual document.
The business must be able to reconstruct the folder structure of the document library, using the recorded depth of each entry in the hierarchy.
Each document has an owner who is an employee.
The business must be able to report on documents by owner, for example to find documents whose owner has left the company.
Employee master data is owned outside the production and product management area and must be sourced from there.
Each document carries a revision number, and the business must be able to see which revision of a document is current.
Each document is associated with an engineering change approval number.
The business must be able to trace documents to the engineering change that authorised them.
Each document has an approval status of Pending approval, Approved or Obsolete.
The business must be able to report on documents by approval status.
The business must be able to find documents pending approval and documents still in circulation that are marked obsolete.
Each document carries a file name and a file extension indicating its type, which the business needs for archiving and access purposes.
Each document has a short abstract or summary, distinct from the full document content, and the summary is what most business reporting needs.
The full binary document content is generally not required in analytical reporting, and its inclusion should be confirmed rather than assumed.
Documents are linked to products: a product may have several associated documents such as assembly instructions, specifications and safety notices, and a document may apply to several products.
The business must be able to identify manufactured products that have no associated document, as a documentation-completeness check.
A product may be assembled from other products, and the business must be able to record, for a given assembly, which products are its components.
Both sides of an assembly relationship are products, and a component in one assembly may itself be an assembly of further components, so the structure is recursive and can be several levels deep.
The business must know, for each component in an assembly, the quantity of that component needed to make one of the assembly item.
The business must know the unit of measure in which the component quantity is expressed, since quantity without unit is not actionable.
The business must know how deep a component sits below its parent assembly, being its level in the bill of materials.
The bill of materials level must support both explosion of a bill of materials to raw components and summary reporting at a chosen level.
Each component-in-assembly relationship carries the date the component started being used in the assembly and the date it stopped being used.
The business must be able to determine what a product was made of on a given date, not only what it is made of now.
The business must be able to identify currently active bill of materials relationships, being those that have started and not yet ended, as the default view for planning and costing.
requirements.obj: currently active bill of materials relationships

requirements.text: The business must be able to see component substitutions over time, where one component stopped being used in an assembly on a date and another started, as a design change visible to engineering and cost teams.
The business must be able to determine, for any component, all the assemblies it is used in (where used), in order to assess the impact of a component shortage, price change or quality problem.
The business must be able to cost an assembly from the costs of its components and the quantities required.
requirements.obj: assembly from component costs and quantities

requirements.text: The business must be able to compare the built-up cost of an assembly with the assembly's recorded standard cost.
requirements.obj: built-up assembly cost against standard cost

requirements.text: The business maintains a standard list of units of measure, each identified by a short code and carrying a descriptive name.
The same standard list of units of measure serves the quantity of a component in an assembly, the unit for a product's size and the unit for a product's weight.
All quantity and dimension reporting must present the unit alongside the figure.
Figures expressed in different units must never be aggregated without conversion.
Whether conversion factors between units of measure exist anywhere in the business needs clarification, as they are not held in this system.
Each manufacturing location (shop floor or work centre within the plant) is identified by a name.
Each location has a standard hourly cost rate.
The business uses the location's standard hourly cost rate to cost the time products spend at that location.
Each location has a stated work capacity expressed in hours.
The business must be able to compare actual hours consumed at a location against its stated capacity in order to identify bottlenecks and under-used capacity.
A location serves two purposes: it is where manufacturing operations are performed and where inventory is held.
Reporting must be able to address both the manufacturing use and the inventory-holding use of the same location.
The business must know the quantity of each product held at each location.
Within a location, stock is stored in a specific shelf, and within a shelf, in a specific bin.
The business must be able to report inventory down to shelf and bin level, as used by stock-picking and stock-counting operations.
requirements.obj: inventory at shelf and bin level

requirements.text: The same product may be held at several locations, and a location may hold many products.
The meaningful inventory fact is the quantity of a given product at a given location in a given shelf and bin.
The business must be able to total inventory for a product across all locations.
The business must be able to total inventory at a location across all products.
The business must be able to value inventory by combining quantities on hand with the applicable standard cost of the product.
The operational system holds only the current inventory position, not a history of it.

The warehouse is expected to build inventory history by capturing the inventory position over time so that inventory levels can be reported as at past dates; this is to be confirmed as a requirement with the supply chain team.
The business raises work orders to manufacture products.
Each work order must be uniquely identifiable.
Each work order must state which product is being made.
Each work order states the quantity ordered.
Each work order records the quantity actually stocked, being the good output that reached inventory.
Each work order records the quantity scrapped.
The business must be able to calculate and report a scrap rate (scrapped quantity against ordered quantity) by product, by product line, by category and over time.
Where a quantity was scrapped, the work order records a scrap reason.
The business maintains a standard list of scrap reasons, each carrying a failure description.
The business must be able to report scrap volumes and scrap costs by scrap reason in order to prioritise quality improvement effort.
requirements.obj: scrap volume and scrap cost by scrap reason

requirements.text: A work order completed without scrap has no scrap reason, so not every work order has a scrap reason.
Reporting must handle work orders that have no scrap reason.
Each work order records a start date, an end date and a due date.
The business must be able to report on manufacturing lead time, measured from start to end of a work order.
The business must be able to report on schedule adherence of work orders, measured as end date against due date.
The business must be able to identify work orders that are open, meaning started but not ended.
The business must be able to identify work orders that are overdue against their due date.
The business must be able to report work order volume and output over time, by product and by product grouping.
Each work order is broken down into a sequence of operations, executed in order.
The business must know the sequence number of each operation, since the order of operations is meaningful.
Each operation is performed at a manufacturing location.
The business must be able to report the manufacturing workload falling on each location.
Each operation carries a scheduled start date and a scheduled end date.
Each operation carries an actual start date and an actual end date.
Both scheduled and actual operation dates must be retained.
The business must be able to report schedule adherence at operation level by comparing scheduled and actual dates.
The business must be able to identify operations that are scheduled but not yet started, started but not yet finished, and completed, based on the presence of the actual dates.
Each operation records the actual resource hours consumed.
The business must be able to compare hours consumed at a location against that location's stated capacity.
Each operation carries a planned cost and an actual cost.
The business must be able to report cost variance at operation level, work order level, product level and location level.
The business must be able to combine actual resource hours with the location's standard hourly cost rate to understand how operation costs arise.
requirements.obj: actual resource hours and location hourly cost rate

requirements.text: The business must be able to reconcile the cost derived from actual hours and hourly rate against the recorded actual cost of the operation.
requirements.obj: derived operation cost against recorded actual cost

requirements.text: The business must be able to roll up all operations of a work order to give a total manufactured cost for that work order.
The business must be able to compare the total manufactured cost of a work order against the standard cost of the product manufactured.
requirements.obj: work order manufactured cost against product standard cost

requirements.text: Each operation identifies the product being manufactured as well as the work order.
The product identified on an operation is expected to agree with the product on its work order, and any disagreement must be flagged as a data quality issue.
requirements.obj: product mismatch between operation and work order

requirements.text: The business maintains a history of standard cost for each product, with a start date and an end date defining the period during which each cost applied.
The business must be able to determine the standard cost that applied to a product on any given date, not just the current cost.
requirements.obj: standard cost on a given date

requirements.text: The current standard cost period is the one with no end date.
The business must be able to identify the currently applicable standard cost for every product.
The business must be able to report cost movements over time, showing how the standard cost of a product, a product line or a category has changed and by how much.
The current product record carries a standard cost figure that is expected to agree with the currently applicable entry in the cost history.
The business must reconcile the product record standard cost against the currently applicable cost history entry and report any disagreement as a data quality issue.
requirements.obj: product standard cost against cost history

requirements.text: Historic transactions must be valued using the cost applicable at the time of the transaction, not today's cost, when analysing margin or manufacturing cost over a period.
The business maintains a history of list price for each product, with a start date and an end date defining the period during which each price applied.
The business must be able to determine the list price that applied to a product on any given date.
requirements.obj: list price on a given date

requirements.text: The current list price period is the one with no end date.
The business must be able to identify the currently applicable list price for every product.
The business must be able to report price movements over time, including frequency, size and direction of price changes by product, product line and category.
The current product record carries a list price that is expected to agree with the currently applicable entry in the price history.
The business must reconcile the product record list price against the currently applicable price history entry.
requirements.obj: product list price against price history

requirements.text: The business must be able to analyse margin over time by combining the list price applicable on a date with the standard cost applicable on the same date.
Cost history and price history are maintained independently and their periods do not necessarily align, so margin analysis must handle overlapping but non-identical periods.
The business must be able to identify each inventory transaction uniquely.
Every movement of stock is recorded as an inventory transaction, forming the movement history behind the current inventory position.
Each inventory transaction states the product involved, the quantity moved, and the date and time it occurred.
Each inventory transaction states its type: work order, sales order or purchase order.
The business must be able to separate manufacturing movements, outbound sales movements and inbound purchase movements by transaction type.
Each inventory transaction refers to the originating order and to the specific line on that order, which is a work order, sales order or purchase order depending on the transaction type.
The business must be able to trace a stock movement back to the document that caused it.
The order reference on a transaction is ambiguous and must always be read together with the transaction type to know which kind of order is meant.
Each inventory transaction carries an actual cost.
The business must be able to value stock movements at the cost actually applied.
The business must be able to report cost of goods manufactured, sold and purchased based on the actual cost of transactions.
requirements.obj: cost of goods manufactured, sold and purchased

requirements.text: The business must be able to reconcile the net effect of transactions for a product against the current inventory quantity held for that product, as a data quality and stock-accuracy control.
requirements.obj: net transaction effect against current inventory quantity

requirements.text: Transactions do not record a location, so movement history is available at product level but not at location level.
If location-level movement analysis is required, the missing location on transactions is a gap that needs to be raised with the operational system owners.
The business must be able to report transaction volume and value over time, by product, product grouping, and transaction type.
Older inventory transactions are moved out of the live operational store into an archive.
The archive holds the same information as the live store: transaction identifier, product, order reference and line, date, type, quantity and actual cost.
The business must be able to see live and archived transactions as one continuous history for long-run historical analysis.
requirements.obj: live and archived transactions as one history

requirements.text: Reporting covering a multi-year period must not look only at the live store, because that would silently under-report.
The business needs clarity, to be established with the operational system owners, on the rule that governs when a transaction is archived.
A transaction must exist in exactly one of the live and archive stores at any time and never be counted twice; this needs confirmation with the operational system owners.
Customers submit reviews of products.
The business must be able to identify each review and know which product it relates to.
Each review records the name of the reviewer, their e-mail address and the date the review was submitted.
Each review carries a rating on a scale of one to five, with five the highest.
Each review carries free-text comments from the reviewer.
The business must be able to report average rating and review volume by product, product model, subcategory and category.
The business must be able to track how ratings move over time.
The business must be able to identify products with consistently low ratings so that quality and product management can act on them.
The business must be able to relate poorly rated products to their scrap and manufacturing cost history.
requirements.obj: poorly rated products to scrap and manufacturing cost history

requirements.text: Reviewer e-mail addresses are personal data, and any use of review data in reporting must respect data protection obligations.
How reviewer identity is handled in analytical reporting must be agreed with the data protection officer before review data is published in reports.
Reviewers are identified only by name and e-mail address, with no link to the customer master.
Whether a reviewer can or should be matched to a known customer is an open question for the customer data owners and is out of scope.
Every record in the operational system carries the date and time it was last updated.
The business must be able to use the last-updated date and time to understand the currency of data and to detect records that have not been maintained.
The business must be able to report the as-at date of any figure presented, so users know what point in time a report reflects.
Analysis of past periods must use the values of bills of materials, standard costs and list prices that applied at the time.
Past-period analysis must not be silently restated when a cost, price or assembly structure changes.
A product may have no subcategory, no model, no photograph, no document, no review, and no bill of materials.
Reporting must treat the absence of optional relationships as legitimate business situations, not as errors.
Reporting must still be able to report absences of optional relationships as completeness gaps where that is the question being asked.
Products to documents, products to photographs, models to illustrations, and models to descriptions by culture are many-to-many relationships.
Each many-to-many association is a business fact in its own right and must be retained as such.
The owner of a document is an employee, and inventory transactions refer to sales orders and purchase orders, which point outside the production area.
These external references must join up with the human resources, sales and purchasing areas of the warehouse when those are built, and until then can only be reported as identifiers.

Which structured-document and binary content (catalogue descriptions, manufacturing instructions, illustration diagrams, photograph images, full document content) is needed for business reporting, and at what level of detail, must be agreed with marketing and manufacturing engineering rather than assumed.
Technical record identifiers in the operational system that have no business meaning should not surface in business reporting.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-002 states the product number is unique and is the natural business key used day-to-day; REQ-001 requires unique identification. Stable, unique, business-recognised and mandatory.
System-generated surrogate identifier; REQ-048-3 says technical identifiers with no business meaning should not surface in reporting. Weak business key, kept only as a source reference.
REQ-004 explicitly states the product name is not unique and must not be relied on to identify a product.
REQ-033 states a product category must be identifiable by its name (e.g. bikes, components, clothing, accessories). Business-recognised; uniqueness is implied but not explicitly stated.
Surrogate identifier with no business meaning (REQ-048-3); weak key.
REQ-034 states a product subcategory must be identifiable by its name. Business-recognised; global uniqueness is not confirmed (REQ-035 notes it belongs to one category).
Surrogate identifier with no business meaning (REQ-048-3); weak key.
REQ-040 states the business must be able to identify a product model by its name. Business-recognised; uniqueness not explicitly stated.
Surrogate identifier with no business meaning (REQ-048-3); weak key.
REQ-049 states each culture is identified by a short culture code. The code is business-assigned, stable and mandatory.
REQ-049 describes name as descriptive only; the code is the identifier.
REQ-095 states each unit of measure is identified by a short code; used across REQ-096 for component quantity, size and weight. Stable, business-recognised and mandatory.
REQ-095 describes the name as descriptive; the code is the identifier.

REQ-048 describes free-text descriptions held independently of any product, with no natural identifier stated in the requirements. The ID is a technical identifier, so it is a weak but only available key.

REQ-054 and REQ-055 describe a photograph library with no natural business identifier stated. The ID is a technical identifier and the only available key. Thumbnail and large file names are possible alternatives but are not stated to be unique.
REQ-061 describes illustrations as technical diagrams with no natural identifier stated. The ID is a technical identifier and the only available key.

REQ-065 requires each document in the hierarchical library (REQ-064, REQ-067) to be identifiable. DocumentNode is the hierarchy path identifier that locates each entry, but it is not explicitly called unique.
System-generated GUID with no business meaning (REQ-048-3); weak alternative key.
REQ-077 says documents carry a file name, but it is not stated to be unique or identifying.
REQ-001-2 states each manufacturing location is identified by a name. Business-recognised and used to refer to shop floor or work centre; uniqueness is implied.
Surrogate identifier with no business meaning (REQ-048-3); weak key.
REQ-026-2 describes a standard list of scrap reasons, each carrying a failure description. The name is the business-recognised label, but uniqueness is not explicitly stated.
Surrogate identifier; the requirements name no other identifier, so it is a weak fallback (REQ-048-3).
REQ-019-2 states each work order must be uniquely identifiable. The ID is the only identifier in the source columns and is business-used for work orders, though it is technically generated.
REQ-036-2, REQ-037-2 and REQ-053-2 state an operation is identified by its work order, product and sequence number, because the order of operations is meaningful. This is a composite key.
REQ-001-3 requires each inventory transaction to be uniquely identifiable. REQ-017-3 lists the transaction identifier as held in both the live and archive stores.
REQ-023-3 requires each review to be identifiable. No natural key is stated: reviewer name and e-mail are personal data (REQ-031-3) and not unique per review, so the review ID is the practical key.
REQ-012-2 states the meaningful inventory fact is the quantity of a given product at a given location, shelf and bin. This is a composite key.

REQ-082, REQ-083 and REQ-088 describe a relationship between an assembly product and a component product, with a start date for the period of use. The requirements state no single identifier, so this is a composite of those elements.

hubs.name: hub_address
hubs.description: Postal address recorded once and shareable by many parties.

hubs.name: hub_address_type
hubs.description: Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping).

hubs.name: hub_contact_type
hubs.description: Reference list of contact roles.

hubs.name: hub_phone_number_type
hubs.description: Reference list of phone number types (home, work, mobile).

hubs.name: hub_country_region
hubs.description: Countries and regions identified by ISO code.

hubs.name: hub_state_province

hubs.name: hub_department

hubs.name: hub_shift

hubs.name: hub_job_candidate

hubs.name: hub_product_subcategory

hubs.name: hub_product_model

hubs.name: hub_culture
hubs.description: Language/locale designation, identified by a short culture code.

hubs.name: hub_unit_measure
hubs.description: Standard unit of measure, identified by a short code.

hubs.name: hub_product_description
hubs.description: Free-text marketing description held in a library, independent of any one product.

hubs.name: hub_product_photo
hubs.description: Photograph in the product photo library.

hubs.name: hub_illustration
hubs.description: Technical diagram used in manufacturing instructions.

hubs.name: hub_document
hubs.description: Entry (document or folder) in the hierarchical controlled document library.

hubs.name: hub_location
hubs.description: Manufacturing location / inventory location. Anchored on the ID because inventory and routing reference locations by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_scrap_reason
hubs.description: Standard scrap reason. Anchored on the ID because WorkOrder references scrap reasons by ID.

hubs.name: hub_work_order
hubs.description: Work order raised to manufacture a product.

hubs.name: hub_inventory_transaction
hubs.description: Inventory transaction (stock movement), fed by both the live and the archive store so they form one continuous history.

hubs.name: hub_product_review
hubs.description: Customer review of a product.

links.name: link_business_entity_job_candidate

links.name: link_product_product_subcategory
links.description: A product belongs to at most one subcategory. The link is optional.

links.name: link_product_subcategory_product_category

links.name: link_product_product_model

links.name: link_product_unit_measure

links.name: link_product_model_description_culture

links.name: link_work_order_product

links.name: link_work_order_scrap_reason

links.name: link_work_order_product_location

links.name: link_inventory_transaction_product
links.description: The product moved by an inventory transaction.

links.name: link_product_review_product
links.description: The product a review relates to.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone_number_type_phones
satellites.description: Telephone numbers of a person per phone type, historised.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of party-address relationships.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_contact_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of contact relationships.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street, city and postal details, historised.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of the address.

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type name.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type name.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State/province code, no-genuine-code flag and name.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift name and start/end times. History is kept because definitions can be adjusted.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_resume
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé, stored as a structured document. It is non-employee personal data, subject to its own retention rules.

satellites.name: sat_product_details
satellites.description: Descriptive product attributes, including the natural product number.

satellites.name: sat_product_pricing

satellites.name: sat_product_inventory_policy

satellites.name: sat_product_lifecycle
satellites.description: Sale availability and discontinuation dates.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle events with their own rate of change.

satellites.name: sat_product_cost_history
satellites.description: Standard cost history periods per product.

satellites.name: sat_product_list_price_history
satellites.description: List price history periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source relation at finer grain (one row per price period).

satellites.name: sat_product_category_details
satellites.description: Category name.

satellites.name: sat_product_subcategory_details
satellites.description: Subcategory name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_details
satellites.description: Product model name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_content
satellites.description: Structured catalogue description and manufacturing instructions.

satellites.name: sat_culture_details
satellites.description: Culture name.

satellites.name: sat_unit_measure_details
satellites.description: Unit of measure name.

satellites.name: sat_product_description_details
satellites.description: Free-text marketing description.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_details

satellites.description: Binary images for the thumbnail and large versions.

satellites.name: sat_illustration_diagram
satellites.description: Structured technical diagram.

satellites.name: sat_document_details
satellites.description: Document metadata: title, folder flag, hierarchy level, revision, engineering change number, approval status, file name and type, and summary. Full binary content is excluded until confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_location_details
satellites.description: Location name, standard hourly cost rate and capacity in hours.

satellites.name: sat_scrap_reason_details
satellites.description: Scrap reason failure description.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_details
satellites.description: Work order quantities and dates.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_product_location_operation
satellites.description: Operation details for each operation sequence: scheduled and actual dates, resource hours and costs.

satellites.name: sat_product_location_inventory
satellites.description: Quantity on hand per shelf and bin. Captured over time to build inventory history.

satellites.name: sat_product_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Flag marking the principal image of the product.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_effectivity
satellites.description: Period during which a component is used in an assembly.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_details
satellites.description: Bill of materials level and component quantity per assembly.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_details
satellites.description: Live-store transaction details. The order reference is kept as an identifier and is read together with the transaction type.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_archive
satellites.description: Archived transaction details, which together with the live store form one continuous history.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source: archive store.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_details
satellites.description: Review date, rating and comments.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_reviewer_pii
satellites.description: Reviewer identity (personal data).

contracts.name: BillOfMaterials

schema.description: Identifier of the parent product (assembly) that the component belongs to; references Product.

schema.description: Identifier of the component product used in the assembly; references Product.

schema.name: StartDate

schema.name: UnitMeasureCode

schema.name: BOMLevel
schema.description: Level of the component within the bill of materials hierarchy.

schema.name: ModifiedDate

contracts.name: Culture

schema.name: ModifiedDate

schema.name: ModifiedDate

contracts.name: Illustration

contracts.name: Location

schema.name: ModifiedDate

contracts.name: WorkOrder

The contract enforces the declared schema, business key and not-null constraints; no value-level thresholds are mandated by the requirements.

schema.name: WorkOrderID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the work order (business key).

schema.name: ProductID
schema.description: Identifier of the product being manufactured; references the Product asset.

schema.name: OrderQty
schema.description: Quantity of the product ordered to be produced on the work order.

schema.name: StockedQty
schema.description: Quantity of the product actually received into inventory from the work order.

schema.name: ScrappedQty
schema.description: Quantity of the product scrapped during manufacturing on the work order.

schema.description: Date and time work on the work order started.

schema.name: EndDate

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: WorkOrderRouting

schema.name: WorkOrderID
schema.description: Identifier of the work order this routing operation belongs to; references the WorkOrder asset.

schema.name: ProductID
schema.description: Identifier of the product being manufactured in this operation; references the Product asset.

schema.name: OperationSequence
schema.description: Sequence number of the manufacturing operation within the work order routing.

schema.name: LocationID
schema.description: Identifier of the manufacturing location where the operation is performed; references the Location asset.

schema.name: ScheduledStartDate
schema.description: Planned start date/time of the operation.

schema.name: ScheduledEndDate
schema.description: Planned end date/time of the operation.

schema.name: ActualStartDate
schema.description: Actual start date/time of the operation; may be absent if the operation has not started.

schema.name: ActualEndDate
schema.description: Actual end date/time of the operation; may be absent if the operation has not completed.

schema.name: ActualResourceHrs
schema.description: Number of resource hours actually used for the operation; may be absent if not yet completed.

schema.name: PlannedCost
schema.description: Estimated cost of the operation.

schema.name: ActualCost
schema.description: Actual cost incurred for the operation; may be absent if not yet completed.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date/time the source record was last modified.

# ADR-0001: Data Vault model derived from requirements

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Decision makers:** Vault-Agent (generated) — pending human review

## Context

This model was derived automatically by the Vault-Agent pipeline from 218 requirement(s) and 29 business key candidate(s). It records the Data Vault 2.0 structures the modeler chose and traces each back to the requirements that justify it.

## Decision

Model the following Data Vault 2.0 structures.

### Hubs (15)

- **hub_product** — business key `ProductID`. Product master. ProductNumber is the business-recognised natural key (REQ-002), but every dependent relation (inventory, work orders, BOM, cost/price history, transactions, reviews, photos, documents) carries only ProductID. The hub is therefore anchored on ProductID so those relations can attach, and ProductNumber is kept as a descriptive attribute. _(requirements: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-048-3)_
- **hub_product_category** — business key `ProductCategoryID`. Top level of the merchandising hierarchy. Anchored on the ID because ProductSubcategory references categories by ID; Name is kept in a satellite. _(requirements: REQ-032, REQ-033)_
- **hub_product_subcategory** — business key `ProductSubcategoryID`. Second level of the merchandising hierarchy. Anchored on the ID because Product references subcategories by ID; Name is kept in a satellite. _(requirements: REQ-032, REQ-034)_
- **hub_product_model** — business key `ProductModelID`. Product model shared by several products. Anchored on the ID because Product and the association tables reference models by ID; Name is kept in a satellite. _(requirements: REQ-040, REQ-041, REQ-044)_
- **hub_culture** — business key `CultureID`. Language/locale designation, identified by a short culture code. _(requirements: REQ-049)_
- **hub_unit_measure** — business key `UnitMeasureCode`. Standard unit of measure, identified by a short code. _(requirements: REQ-095, REQ-096)_
- **hub_product_description** — business key `ProductDescriptionID`. Free-text marketing description held in a library, independent of any one product. _(requirements: REQ-048)_
- **hub_product_photo** — business key `ProductPhotoID`. Photograph in the product photo library. _(requirements: REQ-054, REQ-055)_
- **hub_illustration** — business key `IllustrationID`. Technical diagram used in manufacturing instructions. _(requirements: REQ-061)_
- **hub_document** — business key `DocumentNode`. Entry (document or folder) in the hierarchical controlled document library. _(requirements: REQ-064, REQ-065)_
- **hub_location** — business key `LocationID`. Manufacturing location / inventory location. Anchored on the ID because inventory and routing reference locations by ID; Name is kept in a satellite. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-006-2)_
- **hub_scrap_reason** — business key `ScrapReasonID`. Standard scrap reason. Anchored on the ID because WorkOrder references scrap reasons by ID. _(requirements: REQ-026-2)_
- **hub_work_order** — business key `WorkOrderID`. Work order raised to manufacture a product. _(requirements: REQ-018-2, REQ-019-2)_
- **hub_inventory_transaction** — business key `TransactionID`. Inventory transaction (stock movement), fed by both the live and the archive store so they form one continuous history. Integrated from 2 source(s): TransactionHistory.TransactionID, TransactionHistoryArchive.TransactionID; canonical staging key column `TRANSACTIONID`. _(requirements: REQ-001-3, REQ-002-3, REQ-016-3, REQ-017-3, REQ-018-3)_
- **hub_product_review** — business key `ProductReviewID`. Customer review of a product. _(requirements: REQ-022-3, REQ-023-3)_

### Links (16)

- **link_product_product_subcategory** — connects hub_product, hub_product_subcategory. A product belongs to at most one subcategory. The link is optional. _(requirements: REQ-036, REQ-037, REQ-039)_
- **link_product_subcategory_product_category** — connects hub_product_subcategory, hub_product_category. A subcategory belongs to exactly one category. _(requirements: REQ-035, REQ-039)_
- **link_product_product_model** — connects hub_product, hub_product_model. A product belongs to at most one product model. _(requirements: REQ-041, REQ-042, REQ-043, REQ-044)_
- **link_product_unit_measure** — connects hub_product, hub_unit_measure (size), hub_unit_measure (weight). Units of measure in which a product's size and weight are expressed. _(requirements: REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-096)_
- **link_product_assembly_component** — connects hub_product (assembly), hub_product (component), hub_unit_measure. Bill of materials. An assembly product is made of a component product, with the component quantity expressed in a unit of measure. The structure is recursive. Unit of work: ProductAssemblyID + ComponentID (+ UnitMeasureCode). Driving key: hub_product (assembly), hub_product (component). _(requirements: REQ-082, REQ-083, REQ-085, REQ-088, REQ-092)_
- **link_product_model_description_culture** — connects hub_product_model, hub_product_description, hub_culture. A product model described by a product description in a specific culture. Unit of work: ProductModelID + ProductDescriptionID + CultureID. _(requirements: REQ-050, REQ-051, REQ-052, REQ-053, REQ-043-3, REQ-044-3)_
- **link_product_model_illustration** — connects hub_product_model, hub_illustration. Many-to-many association of illustrations with product models. _(requirements: REQ-062, REQ-063, REQ-043-3)_
- **link_product_product_photo** — connects hub_product, hub_product_photo. Many-to-many association of products with photographs. _(requirements: REQ-056, REQ-059, REQ-043-3)_
- **link_product_document** — connects hub_product, hub_document. Many-to-many association of products with documents. _(requirements: REQ-080, REQ-081, REQ-043-3)_
- **link_document_business_entity** — connects hub_document, hub_business_entity. Document owner. The owner is an employee held in the existing HR hub (Document.Owner maps to BusinessEntityID). _(requirements: REQ-068, REQ-069, REQ-070, REQ-045-3, REQ-046-3)_
- **link_product_location** — connects hub_product, hub_location. Inventory: a product held at a location (many-to-many). _(requirements: REQ-008-2, REQ-011-2, REQ-012-2, REQ-013-2, REQ-014-2)_
- **link_work_order_product** — connects hub_work_order, hub_product. The product a work order manufactures. _(requirements: REQ-020-2, REQ-035-2)_
- **link_work_order_scrap_reason** — connects hub_work_order, hub_scrap_reason. Scrap reason recorded on a work order. The link is optional. _(requirements: REQ-025-2, REQ-027-2, REQ-028-2)_
- **link_work_order_product_location** — connects hub_work_order, hub_product, hub_location. Work order routing: operations of a work order for a product, performed at a manufacturing location. Unit of work: WorkOrderID + ProductID + LocationID (operation sequence as dependent key). _(requirements: REQ-036-2, REQ-038-2, REQ-039-2, REQ-053-2)_
- **link_inventory_transaction_product** — connects hub_inventory_transaction, hub_product. The product moved by an inventory transaction. _(requirements: REQ-003-3, REQ-012-3, REQ-015-3)_
- **link_product_review_product** — connects hub_product_review, hub_product. The product a review relates to. _(requirements: REQ-023-3, REQ-027-3)_

### Satellites (29)

- **sat_product_details** — on hub_product; payload: ProductNumber, Name, MakeFlag, FinishedGoodsFlag, Color, Size, Weight, DaysToManufacture, ProductLine, Class, Style, ModifiedDate. Descriptive product attributes, including the natural product number. Split rationale: Slowly changing descriptive classification of the product.. _(requirements: REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-005, REQ-007, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-012, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-017, REQ-019, REQ-020)_
- **sat_product_pricing** — on hub_product; payload: StandardCost, ListPrice. Current standard cost and list price. Split rationale: Financial figures that change at a different rate from descriptive attributes.. _(requirements: REQ-021, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-060-2, REQ-068-2)_
- **sat_product_inventory_policy** — on hub_product; payload: SafetyStockLevel, ReorderPoint. Inventory planning parameters. Split rationale: Supply-chain planning parameters, maintained separately.. _(requirements: REQ-024, REQ-025, REQ-026)_
- **sat_product_lifecycle** — on hub_product; payload: SellStartDate, SellEndDate, DiscontinuedDate. Sale availability and discontinuation dates. Split rationale: Lifecycle events with their own rate of change.. _(requirements: REQ-027, REQ-028, REQ-029, REQ-030, REQ-031)_
- **sat_product_cost_history** — on hub_product; payload: EndDate, StandardCost, ModifiedDate. Standard cost history periods per product. Multi-active satellite, child dependent key: StartDate. Source table: ProductCostHistory. Split rationale: Separate source relation at finer grain (one row per cost period).. _(requirements: REQ-055-2, REQ-056-2, REQ-057-2, REQ-058-2, REQ-059-2, REQ-061-2, REQ-062-2)_
- **sat_product_list_price_history** — on hub_product; payload: EndDate, ListPrice, ModifiedDate. List price history periods per product. Multi-active satellite, child dependent key: StartDate. Source table: ProductListPriceHistory. Split rationale: Separate source relation at finer grain (one row per price period).. _(requirements: REQ-063-2, REQ-064-2, REQ-065-2, REQ-066-2, REQ-067-2, REQ-069-2, REQ-070-2, REQ-071-2)_
- **sat_product_category_details** — on hub_product_category; payload: Name, ModifiedDate. Category name. _(requirements: REQ-033)_
- **sat_product_subcategory_details** — on hub_product_subcategory; payload: Name, ModifiedDate. Subcategory name. _(requirements: REQ-034)_
